title: Causal latency-slice explorer and trace-hook adapter for multi-signal failure attribution
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: On recent incidents we lacked a way to quickly map increased tail latency or error spikes to their causal signal (overload, transport errors, model failures, or client retries). Current dashboards slice by service and endpoint but do not correlate normalized failure classes with trace-level evidence or with metric pipelines that translate HTTP/gRPC codes and model responses into canonical categories.

Goal: Build a lightweight trace-hook adapter and an interactive explorer dashboard that joins three signals: span-level traces, metric-derived failure counts, and normalized log/error fields from the logging pipeline. The output should let on-call and SRE teams answer: 'Is this spike caused by upstream timeouts, internal queueing/overload, model decode errors, or client mis-use?' within 2 clicks and support drill-to-trace.

Scope:
- A small, language-agnostic trace-hook adapter (service-side library + sidecar shim) that attaches normalized attributes to spans: failure.class, failure.subclass, upstream_latency_ms, kvcache_hit, model_variant, http_status_family.
- Pipeline mapping rules in metric/log ingestion to normalize HTTP/gRPC codes and model response errors into taxonomy buckets: timeout, overload/backpressure, model-runtime-error, model-output-quality, protocol-error (4xx/5xx), partial-response.
- Explorer dashboard UI that shows causal slices: latency distribution by failure.class, SLI exposure by route, trace-sample list with enriched attrs, and an «impact timeline» mapping metric anomalies to correlated trace evidence.

Non-goals: Full auto-root-cause or machine learning classification of every incident. This ticket delivers the adapter and the first-pass dashboard and pipeline rules; ML-driven classifiers are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-hook adapter available as a small SDK/shim with documented install for Node, Go, and Python
Span attributes emitted: failure.class, failure.subclass, upstream_latency_ms, kvcache_hit, model_variant, protocol_status_family
Ingestion pipeline transforms map common HTTP/gRPC codes and Redwood model errors to the canonical taxonomy described in the doc
Dashboard contains: causal slice view (by failure.class), per-route SLI exposure table, sample traces linked to logs, and an impact timeline showing metric -> trace correlation
Dashboard queries complete within 5s for 30d-7d ranges using current ClickHouse/ES retention and the default index patterns
Rollout plan and sampling budget documented; added to runtime-1.18 rollout checklist
Automated tests for pipeline mapping rules and unit tests for trace-hook adapter added in CI
On-call runbook updated with how-to use the explorer for P1 latency or error investigations
work_items: Design failure taxonomy mapping doc and publish to Confluence
Implement trace-hook adapter APIs and sidecar shim for attribute enrichment
Add transform rules to metrics/log ingestion (Logstash/Vector/Fluentd config snippets)
Build dashboard panels and new queries in Grafana/Console: causal-slice, SLI-table, trace-sampler list, impact timeline
Create sampling policy: low-latency tail sampling + error-biased capture; instrument cost estimate
End-to-end test with synthetic workload (timeout, overload, model-exception) and validate slices
Rollout first to staging, then 10% of production services, monitor observability cost and adjust sampling

comments: 2025-02-14 Miguel Ortega: Scoped initial prototype for Node and Go adapter. Plan to ship Python next sprint. Est: 5 points.
2025-02-18 Sofia Reed (PM): Prioritize failure.class mapping for model errors (runtime exception vs soft decode failure). Need list of model error enums by 2/21.

2025-02-22 Engineering review: Trade-off noted: adding attributes to every span increases span size and storage. Decision: emit attributes only on error spans and tail-sampled spans; provide sidecar to attach metrics for aggregate pipelines.

2025-03-01 QA: End-to-end tests for timeout and model-runtime-error passed in staging. Observability cost projection +12% on trace storage at 10% rollout; acceptable for launch.
